drivingQuestion: Did we learn 'and plasters with lime' or 'or plasters with lime'?
outcomeNote: The dilemma is pursued in the next unit.

segments.he: וְסָד בְּסִיד. אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: ״וְסָד בְּסִיד״ תְּנַן, אוֹ דִילְמָא ״אוֹ סָד בְּסִיד״ תְּנַן?
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that one who digs a pit must distance it three handbreadths from another’s property and «plaster» it «with lime. A dilemma was raised before» the Sages: What is the precise wording of the mishna? «Did we learn: And plasters with lime,» meaning that the walls must be plastered with lime in addition to distancing the pit three handbreadths, «or perhaps we learned: Or plasters with lime,» i.e., one may plaster the walls with lime instead of digging the pit at a distance of three handbreadths.
